page: Microsoft Azure E4as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, with support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, multi-threaded scaling presents a notable tradeoff; multi-core stress-ng CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into average or weak categories. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, consistently perform in the average tier. Large language model inference is viable for small 135M models but drops to poor or weak tiers when processing medium 7B models.

This server does not include local storage, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing external disk attachment. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density relative to the 4 vCPUs provides a resource-dense profile for memory-bound applications without requiring payment for excess compute cores. The virtual machine is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators. It is best suited for memory-intensive workloads such as relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and moderate data-processing tasks that benefit from high single-core speed and a large memory footprint.
description: Microsoft Azure E4as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Easv7 family, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor running at 4.5 GHz, it delivers top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and compression benchmarks. However, multi-threaded scaling is a tradeoff, with multi-core CPU performance and medium-model LLM inference falling into average to poor tiers. The server lacks local storage but supports Premium Storage, and it contains no GPU accelerators. With a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, this configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. It is highly suited for database operations, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing.
